name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,616

clue.text: Rich cake found back in imperial Ceylon

indicators.note: something found has been discovered tucked away inside, so the letters lie within the following words
going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A luxurious cake discovered in colonial-era Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside impeRIAL CEylon sit RIALCE; read backwards they spell ECLAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, a sweet and indulgent kind of small cake.

clue.text: Endless trash with politico orchestrating unrest Stateside

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
orchestrating means arranging parts into a new score, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word minus its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician stirring up trouble in America, with a dig at them as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAS plus POLITICO rearranged gives CAPITOL RIOTS, the attack on the US Congress building in January 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2021 storming of the Washington legislature building was a notorious episode of violent American civil disorder.

clue.text: Sailors trick the German one doing runner

blocks.note: ABs are able seamen
a con is a swindle
DER is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Seamen play a trick on a German who is running away.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do a runner' is British slang for leaving without paying or fleeing; 'the German' is a standard way to clue a German article.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who absconds slips away secretly to escape, which is exactly what bolting from a debt or arrest involves.

clue.text: See 2
Knowing quality, island invested in SA currency

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
pence are coins of British money
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Wisdom shown in putting an island's money into South African currency.
explanation.walkthrough: SA looks like South Africa, inviting the rand, but those two letters are simply taken as written; the currency is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapience is wisdom or discernment, the mental faculty of understanding things deeply.

clue.text: See 19
Perhaps let in respected person coming to office

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version among many, so these letters can take another order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone respected is allowed to take up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge in the sentence but tells you to rearrange the fourteen letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A president-elect has won the vote but not yet been sworn in, so they are about to take up the post.

clue.text: See 6
Smile after tea shows anything but delight

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind another in the order of the answer

blocks.note: cha is British slang for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A grin after teatime that is far from happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The smile comes second because it is 'after' the tea; CHA (also char) is old British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or humiliation, an emotion at the opposite end from pleasure or joy.

clue.text: Knock back drink in old church and head for bishop's office

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the opposite way, so the letters run right to left
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
CE stands for the Church of England
to sip is to drink a little
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Downing a drink in an ancient church before heading for the bishop's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back drink' reads as gulping alcohol, but 'knock back' turns round the drink together with the old church around it; the head follows unreversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The episcopate is the rank, term or jurisdiction held by a bishop, from the Greek word for overseer.

clue.text: Value reflected in welcoming a wronged brother

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: use means value, as in 'of no use'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Worth is shown in making a wronged sibling welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: USE turned round is ESU, which then takes in A; in Genesis, Esau was cheated of his birthright and blessing by his twin Jacob.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Jacob tricked his elder twin out of their father's blessing, so this sibling is the classic injured party.

clue.text: Gadget used in steamship to make furniture

indicators.note: something used in a thing is placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a tool is a gadget
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A device used aboard a steamer to build furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The steamship abbreviation is the prefix on ship names, as in SS Great Britain, and its two letters split to hold the gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Stools are backless seats, a common kind of household item one sits on.

clue.text: Spray with greater frequency to cover rumpled suit

indicators.note: rumpled cloth is creased out of shape, so the letters are disordered
covering something means wrapping around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: more often means with greater frequency
the four letters reordered

explanation.surface: Spraying a creased suit more often to smooth it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for fine droplets; 'with greater frequency' is MORE, which wraps the rearranged SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spray is liquid in fine droplets, and moisture is a general word for dampness or wetness in the air.

clue.text: In seed case find large bluebottle

indicators.note: being in something places it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a pod holds peas or beans
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big blowfly discovered inside a seed pod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' looks like the fly, but it is old British slang for a police officer (from the blue uniform), and PLOD is another British slang term for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British slang for a uniformed police constable, PLOD coming from Mr Plod in the Noddy books.

clue.text: Oily substance from tree put in ground with nitrogen

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An oil from a tree planted in soil with fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree put in ground' reads as planting, but 'ground' means crushed, and 'tree' is part of the letters to rearrange, along with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a volatile resinous oil distilled from pine trees, used as a paint thinner.

clue.text: Toy-boy with gun splattered right-wing commentator

indicators.note: something splattered is scattered in all directions, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written without the hyphen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young lover with a gun shoots a conservative pundit.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby Young is a British journalist and author, known for conservative columns and founding the Free Speech Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Young writes opinion pieces for the Spectator and other publications with a conservative political outlook.

clue.text: Develops liking for Calvin Klein? Assess situation

blocks.note: takes to means comes to like
CK is the designer's initials and brand logo

explanation.surface: Someone grows fond of a designer label, then weighs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes to' is the idiom for beginning to like something; the fashion brand's initials complete it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is an idiom meaning to pause and review the circumstances before deciding.

clue.text: Thrown together, German joins the Italian in bar

indicators.note: being in something places it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Jerry is old British slang for a German
bar and but both mean except
IL is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German teams up with an Italian in a pub, all hastily assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but means 'except'. Jerry was wartime British slang for a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry-built describes something constructed cheaply and badly, slapped up in a hurry with poor materials.

clue.text: Test regularly applied for instance

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an exam is a test
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A test that is applied consistently, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' looks like a single phrase meaning 'e.g.', but 'for' is only the link and 'instance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating a general point, which is what an example offers.

clue.text: Sloth and one near it on the move

indicators.note: things on the move are shifting about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sloth with someone close by, both moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a sloth, the animal, is never on the move; here 'Sloth' means laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, and inertia is a tendency to stay inactive and resist change or effort.

clue.text: Dreadful mistake: error banning old Labour leader

indicators.note: something dreadful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
banning something keeps it out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its O
O is the abbreviation for old; it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a terrible blunder by a party leader who has broken with the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from MISTAKE ERROR and rearrange the eleven letters left. Keir Starmer led the UK Labour Party from 2020 and became Prime Minister in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Starmer succeeded Jeremy Corbyn as head of Britain's main centre-left party in 2020.

clue.text: Saint removed from evil church feature in fire

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: sin is wickedness
S is the abbreviation for saint; it is the letter dropped
a spire tops a church tower

explanation.surface: A saint is rescued from wickedness as a church goes up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fire' reads as burning, but 'in' is only the link; 'fire' is a verb meaning to fill with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir their enthusiasm, the same as stimulating them to act.

clue.text: Gutter spout from glory age renovated

indicators.note: a renovated building has been remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drainpipe fixture salvaged from a building's heyday and restored.
explanation.walkthrough: The restoration image fits the answer, a carved feature of old churches often renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque that carries rainwater from a roof gutter away from the walls.

clue.text: Supplied Liberal with hammer

blocks.note: gave means provided
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is handed a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: L for Liberal is a standard party abbreviation in British politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is a small wooden mallet that judges, auctioneers and chairs strike to call order.

clue.text: Give aid to guitar player having missed intro

indicators.note: missing the introduction means losing the start, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a bassist plays bass guitar

explanation.surface: Helping out a guitarist who came in late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guitar player' could be many things; only BASSIST loses one letter to leave a word meaning help.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to help or support them in doing something.

clue.text: Recalling battlefield doctor for mission?

blocks.note: a la means in the style of, so reminiscent of
MO is a military medical officer

explanation.surface: Reminiscing about an army medic who served on a dangerous assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling' looks like a reversal signal but means 'reminiscent of', the French a la. The question mark marks a definition by example: the Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission and a famous battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was founded as a Spanish Catholic mission in San Antonio before its famous 1836 siege.

clue.text: Black marketeer dignitaries turned around

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: Important people are converted into an illicit trader.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang, especially of the wartime years, for a flashy small-time dealer in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Spivs sold rationed or stolen goods illegally during and after the Second World War in Britain.

clue.text: Radical junior in charge too high to catch?

blocks.note: an ultra is an extremist
a son is often called junior
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An extreme young person in command is too lofty to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too high to catch' sounds like a ball out of reach, but it means a pitch too high for the human ear to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic sound has a frequency above the upper limit of human hearing, so the ear cannot pick it up.

clue.text: Itching to see Indian city with unlimited enchantments

definitions.note: the clue gives a symptom; the answer is the disease, a noun

indicators.note: without limits means without boundaries, so the outside letters are lost

blocks.note: spells, minus first and last letters
Agra is home to the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Eager to visit an Indian city full of endless magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itching to see' reads as eager to visit, but 'Itching' alone is the definition and 'to see' just links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellagra is a niacin-deficiency disease whose symptoms include dermatitis, with rough, irritated skin.

clue.text: Archipelago or island around north

indicators.note: going around something encircles it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
a key is a low island or reef
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Choosing between a group of islands and one island near the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A key (or cay) is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys. Orkney is an island group off the north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney comprises around seventy islands, making it a group of islands, which is what an archipelago is.
